issues_for_lead: Earlier attempt: its local image jakub-netflow-agent-goflow2:v2.2.7-local was built from source (upstream git tag v2.2.7 compiled to a binary, copied into alpine:3.20). It was not a downloaded binary. I removed it and the scratch folder jakub-netflow-img. The compose file and the end-to-end run use the published netsampler/goflow2:v2.2.7@sha256:b8fdc8f3... (pulled after one Docker Hub 429). I kept that 45 MB image on the host so the compose file can be run again; remove it if disk is needed. Source checkout left in scratchpad/jakub-netflow-dl.

Spec difference (JAK-10 step 3): NetflowAdapter.accepts() also accepts a single goflow2 JSON file, recognised by its first line (at most 64 KiB read). Reason: the dashboard upload and /api/ingest save uploads under a random name with no suffix, so a folder can never arrive that way. Without this the 'How to test: flows on the timeline page' step could not work. A .zip of a goflow2 folder still goes to ZeekLogAdapter (it matches .zip by suffix) and gives an empty analysis. The docs should say 'upload the single .json flow file, not a zip'.

app.py's 400 message 'not a .pcap/.pcapng capture or a .zip/.tar.gz of Zeek logs' does not mention goflow2 flow files now. Suggest adding 'or a goflow2 NetFlow/IPFIX JSON file' (I did not edit app.py).

Contract note (JAK-10 step 4): normalize.py now sets source 'netflow' for conn.log records with mg_source 'netflow'. pipeline's default sensor_id for netflow input is 'import' (not 'pcap'). The pull request needs the contract-change label, review by Jaiden and approval by the Security Lead.

Flow-only data fires no rule. A flow to port 23 is not reported as cleartext.telnet because the rules need Zeek's protocol evidence. The asset inventory is empty for flow-only input because inventory.build reads only known_hosts/known_services/software. If assets from flows are wanted, that is a change in Jakub's inventory.py (needs a decision). baseline.new_service keys on (port, proto, service): flows have service '', so mixing a Zeek-learned baseline with NetFlow input would report every service as new. Fiona should know this.

NetFlow v5 ICMP: the adapter decodes the type and code from dst_port (type*256+code). I verified that goflow2 passes the value through unchanged, but I found no primary source for the exporter convention itself. The code comment calls it what exporters do. Please confirm or soften it in the docs.

JAK-11 design choices to put in the guide: (1) Windows pktmon rotates only by size, so the agent stops and restarts pktmon every rotate_seconds, which leaves a gap of under a second between files. (2) tcpdump is started with TZ=UTC because it fills the -w pattern with localtime(). (3) capture_user is required on Linux/macOS (-Z). Debian builds of tcpdump may already drop to a 'tcpdump' user by default (the man page says this can be a compile-time default), so the spool folder must be writable by whoever writes the files. (4) A file counts as uploaded only after a 2xx and then moves to spool/uploaded/ (newest 4 kept). 400/413 go to rejected/. Everything else is retried, oldest first. (5) The config file must be chmod 600 or the agent refuses it.

Security note for the docs: port 8001 is plain HTTP, so the agent's Bearer token and the captures cross the LAN unencrypted. The agent docstring says to use a trusted network. TLS on the ingest port may deserve a GitHub Discussion.

The flow generator (send_flows.py: NetFlow v5 + v9 + IPFIX, documentation addresses only) has no owned path in the repo. The full source is in docs-draft/netflow-agent-notes.md and scratchpad/jakub-netflow-work2/send_flows.py. The lead may want it at scripts/send_test_flows.py.
tests/fixtures/netflow/goflow2.json is real goflow2 v2.2.7 output from the generator, with sampler_address changed from the Docker address 172.18.0.3 to 203.0.113.1. All addresses are RFC 5737.
doc_notes: JAK-10: goflow2 (netsampler/goflow2:v2.2.7 pinned by digest, BSD-3-Clause, amd64+arm64) listens on UDP 2055 (NetFlow v5/v9/IPFIX only, no sFlow) and writes JSON lines to /data/netflow/goflow2.json. It runs as 1000:1000 with a read-only root file system, all capabilities dropped and its HTTP server off (-addr=). The port is published only on MAXGUARD_NETFLOW_ADDRESS, which is required. Never use the 'latest' tag: it is v1.3.8. To rotate, mv the file and send SIGHUP (docker compose kill -s HUP goflow2); goflow2 reopens a fresh file. NetflowAdapter turns each flow into a conn.log line: ts = flow start, uid = 'N' + 17 hex digits of SHA-256 of the record without time_received_ns (deterministic, same length as a Zeek uid), orig_bytes = the flow's bytes, resp_bytes = 0 because a flow is one direction, ICMP type/code go in the ports as in Zeek, plus mg_source 'netflow'. Records that appear twice are written once, a half-written last line is skipped, and the output is sorted, so the same files always give the same conn.log. accepts() never takes a Zeek folder (it has conn.log), a sensor folder (it has zeek/), eve.json or a pcap; NetflowAdapter is last in ADAPTERS. Why no alerts: flows carry no payload, and every MaxGuard rule needs payload evidence from Zeek or Suricata, so flows only feed the timeline (later baselines and block previews). Gotcha: with sampling_rate > 1 the byte counts are sampled. JAK-11: maxguard/sensor/agent.py reads a TOML config outside the repo (~/.config/maxguard/agent.toml, chmod 600), builds `tcpdump [-i IF] -n -G N -w SPOOL/capture-%Y%m%d-%H%M%S.pcap -Z USER` (run with TZ=UTC) or, on Windows, `pktmon start --capture --comp nics --pkt-size 0 --file-name X.etl` / `pktmon stop` / `pktmon etl2pcap X.etl --out X.pcapng`. It uploads every finished file (never the newest while capturing) to <console>/api/ingest as multipart 'file' + 'sensor_id' with an 'Authorization: Bearer' header. `python -m maxguard.sensor.agent --config FILE --upload-only` uploads once without capturing, which is good for a first test. The console must be the user's own machine, and ingest is off (404) unless MAXGUARD_INGEST_TOKEN (at least 32 characters) is set there. Tests never start a capture: they compare the command lists and upload to a ThreadingHTTPServer on 127.0.0.1 and to create_ingest_app through TestClient. Full commands and real output are in docs-draft/netflow-agent-notes.md.
